budget_note: one attempt = one full episode with one candidate; a request stops early on the first attempt that passes
candidates_note: (target_lo_n, target_hi_n) of the contact-feedback grip. Identical set for both groups.

group_A.bias_note: the direction of this order favours low-force requests and penalises high-force ones; the request set spans both directions on purpose, but the baseline order remains a design choice and is reported as such
group_A.name: fixed order
group_A.order: the candidate list above, as written (ascending target_lo_n, then target_hi_n)

group_B.name: retrieval by measured response
group_B.no_write_back: the library is frozen before the trials; no trial result is added to it during the comparison
rule: 1. candidate pool and budget are identical to group A; only the ORDER differs
2. for each candidate (lo, hi), predict the measured hold interval [hold_min, hold_max] from the frozen experience library
3. record selection: records of the SAME object name with measurement_valid and grasp_stable; if fewer than 2, fall back to the same task (any object); if still fewer than 2, all records
4. among the selected records prefer those with the same target_hi_n; if none has it, use all selected
5. predict by piecewise-linear interpolation of hold_min and hold_max against target_lo_n over the selected records (clamped to the nearest record outside the observed range)

6. order: first the candidates whose predicted interval lies inside the requested band, by descending margin to the band edges; then the rest, by ascending distance from the predicted interval centre to the band centre
7. ties are broken by the group A order

manner_requests.text: hold the object with a very light grip
hold the object with a moderate grip
hold the object with a firm grip
hold the object with a very firm grip

manner_requests_note: the four bands are declared here before any trial is run; they are NOT the calibration bands, so no candidate is known in advance to satisfy any of them. A request may turn out to be unsatisfiable by every candidate; such requests are kept and reported, not replaced.
n_requests_detail: 2 tasks x 1 requested object x 4 manner requests x 4 inits

pass_criterion.definition: task_ok AND measurement_valid AND grasp_stable AND hold_min >= band_lo AND hold_max <= band_hi, for the requested object only
pass_criterion.explicitly_not: this is a DEVELOPMENT criterion. It is not a qualified-demonstration yield: it contains no contact-policy verdict, no stage-speed check, no pair logic and no safety conclusion.
pass_criterion.judge: scripts/mt/s8_task_force.py per_object() (unchanged) on the executed episode
pass_criterion.name: task_and_force_band_checks_passed

question: Does retrieval over previously MEASURED responses let the system pick a grip parameter that satisfies a requested hold-force band in fewer attempts than a fixed-order search over the same candidate set?

reported_separately.contact_policy_passed: frozen contact_audit policy (non-fingertip robot body vs movable object above 0.1 N is forbidden), recorded per attempt; on T0/T7 earlier runs this policy did not pass, so it is expected to be 0 and must never be merged into the pass criterion

scope.inits_reason: reserved split 22-39; 22-25 already consumed by earlier work; 30-39 stay unused; holdout 40-49 untouched; calibration inits 8-13 and dev inits 0-7/14-21 are NOT used so that the experience library (built from 8-13) and the test are on different initial states
scope.other_object_fixed_plan_reason: the non-requested object must not vary between groups; the gentlest named plan is used for it in every episode of both groups
scope.requested_object_reason: calibration_usable == true in the frozen v3 calibration; alphabet_soup is calibration_usable == false (grasp_stability_failed) and is NEVER the subject of a request
